steps.title: AO6 Requirement
steps.body: Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation. Spelling errors can cost you marks across all writing questions.

steps.title: Exceptions to remember
steps.body: weird, seize, neither, either, foreign, height, their, heir

steps.title: English Terms
steps.body: metaphor, simile, personification, alliteration, onomatopoeia, juxtaposition, semantic field, foreshadowing, narrative, perspective

steps.title: Tip
steps.body: When in doubt, write the word down. Often your eye will catch an error that your brain misses.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Which is correct: "their book" or "there book"? | Spell the word meaning "to influence": affect or effect? | What is the correct spelling: neccessary or necessary?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: "their book" - their shows possession (belonging to them) | "affect" - affect is the verb meaning to influence | necessary - one c, two s

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Proofread your work - leave 2-3 minutes at the end Circle words you're unsure about and come back to them Use alternative words if you can't spell something Memorise the top 10 commonly misspelt words Practise homophones - they catch many students out Check subject-specific vocabulary in context
